title: Ex-Pakistan Selector Blasts Young Cricketers for Being 'Focused on Money'
excerpt: A former PCB chief selector has slammed Pakistan's young cricketers for prioritizing earnings over developing their game, invoking India's late Bishan Singh Bedi as an example of selfless dedication to cricket.
body:
• A former Pakistan Cricket Board chief selector accused young Pakistani players of being "more focused on earning money" than improving their skills
  • The ex-selector invoked India's legendary spinner Bishan Singh Bedi as a model of dedication to the craft of cricket over financial gain
  • The criticism comes amid Pakistan's ongoing struggles in international cricket and debates about the PCB's new format-based central contracts
  • Pakistan recently introduced format-specific contracts with significantly higher pay — up to PKR 5 million monthly for top Test players

A former Pakistan Cricket Board chief selector has launched a scathing attack on the country's young cricketers, accusing them of being "more focused on earning money" than developing their game, according to the Times of India and NDTV.

The ex-selector pointed to India's legendary left-arm spinner Bishan Singh Bedi as a counterexample — a cricketer who dedicated himself entirely to the art and craft of the game rather than pursuing financial rewards. Bedi, who passed away in October 2023 at the age of 77, was revered across the cricketing world for his uncompromising commitment to the sport and his willingness to speak truth to power.

Pakistan's Money Problem

The former chief selector's comments come at a time when Pakistan cricket is grappling with both underperformance on the field and a fundamental restructuring of how players are compensated. The PCB recently introduced format-based central contracts — a first in Pakistan cricket — with significantly higher pay packages designed to attract the best talent to Test cricket.

Under the new system, players in the top track earn monthly retainers of up to PKR 4.8–5 million and match fees of around PKR 1.5 million for Test matches, a substantial increase from the previous PKR 800,000 match fee. T20-only players receive retainers of PKR 1.2–1.5 million per month.

But critics argue the increased money has not translated into better performances. Instead, the ex-selector suggested, it has created a generation of players who view cricket primarily as a vehicle for wealth rather than a calling.

"Young players are more focused on earning money than on improving their game. Look at someone like Bishan Singh Bedi — he lived and breathed cricket. That kind of dedication is missing."

— Former PCB Chief Selector

The Bedi Standard

The invocation of Bishan Singh Bedi is particularly striking given the historical rivalries between Indian and Pakistani cricket. Bedi played 67 Tests for India, taking 266 wickets with his elegant left-arm spin. He was known for prioritizing the art of bowling over statistics, famously declaring innings closed rather than allowing runs to be scored off poor bowling during a Test match against the West Indies in 1976.

Former Pakistan captain Mushtaq Muhammad, who played alongside Bedi at Northamptonshire for six years in English county cricket, recently spoke of the Indian spinner's profound influence on his career. "When Bishan saw me playing, he said you have got a great ability to bowl," Mushtaq recalled. "He used to spend time with me in the nets. He would tell me 'don't get scared if you are hit for a six as a leg-spinner.'"

Bedi's relationship with Pakistani cricketers transcended national rivalries — a contrast to today's more commercially driven landscape.

Franchise Cricket's Influence

The ex-selector's criticism reflects a broader concern in cricket that the proliferation of franchise leagues — particularly the Indian Premier League and Pakistan's own PSL — has shifted young players' priorities toward short-format earnings at the expense of Test cricket development. Pakistani players can earn substantial sums through franchise contracts, endorsements, and central contracts, with top cricketers potentially earning upward of $100,000 annually.

Pakistan cricket has faced particular challenges in recent years, with inconsistent performances across formats and frequent changes in coaching and selection leadership. The PCB has undergone multiple restructurings, with Iqbal Qasim, Abdul Qadir, and several others cycling through the chief selector role amid constant debates about merit, politics, and priorities.

What It Means for India-Pakistan Cricket

For the Indian diaspora, the story underscores the enduring cultural significance of cricket as more than a sport in the subcontinent. The invocation of Bedi — an Indian icon — by a Pakistani cricket official highlights how the game's greatest figures transcend national boundaries while also serving as a measuring stick for cricket's evolving values.
